flagged.evidence: The remark says energy is defined when “at least one” of the positive and negative kernel integrals is finite, with value in (-infinity,+infinity]. Let rho_n be normalized arclength on the circle of radius 1/4 centered at e^n, and let sigma be the probability mixture with weights proportional to 1/n^2. Distinct circles are more than distance 1 apart, so the positive-part integral is only the same-circle contribution and is finite (each same-circle integral is log 4, weighted by a summable multiple of 1/n^4). For n<m, cross-circle distances are at least e^m/2, so the negative-part integral is bounded below by a positive multiple of sum_m (m-log 2)/m^2 times sum_{n<m}1/n^2, which diverges. Thus one part is finite, as the stated criterion allows, but the energy is -infinity, outside the claimed range.

The Statement quantifies over “every compact L” and writes sup over z in L, without requiring L to be nonempty or defining an empty-set supremum. The empty set is compact; its real supremum is undefined, and the extended-real convention gives -infinity rather than a nonnegative error tending to zero. The proof's maximum and finite-net steps also use nonemptiness.

flagged.evidence: The Remark says Q is “+infinity exactly where the difference fails to tend to 0.” Step 7.1 proves blow-up on P only, and the cited Evans-measure result guarantees U^sigma=+infinity on P without controlling points outside P. For example, on the unit circle let P={a_n=e^(i e^(-4^n))}, xi=1, and sigma=sum_n 2^(-n) delta_{a_n}. This finite measure is carried by the countable polar set P and has U^sigma=+infinity at every a_n, but also U^sigma(1)>=sum_n 2^(-n) log(1/|1-a_n|)=+infinity although 1 is not in P. The stated Evans-measure properties therefore allow Q to blow up at xi, where the difference tends to 0 by the definition of P; they do not license “exactly.”
